title: TRACE: Turn-Level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
hook: A failed agent rollout might still contain dozens of genuinely useful actions — outcome-only RL punishes every one of them the same as the final mistake. TRACE assigns credit per tool call instead, with no extra critic.
key_points: Targets credit assignment for multi-turn agents whose trajectories span tens to hundreds of tool calls before a final answer.
Outcome-only rewards get sparse and high-variance over long trajectories, and mislabel useful early actions in a rollout that ultimately fails.
TRACE represents rollouts as state transitions at tool-call boundaries and gets gold-answer log-probabilities from a frozen reference model.
Those log-probabilities become log-ratio state values; per-action rewards are the Temporal-Difference change in that value between turns — no extra critic or process-label training needed.
On the closed-web BrowseComp-Plus benchmark, TRACE raises Qwen3-4B from 7.2 to 35.6 and Qwen3-30B-A3B from 8.4 to 42.6, using pure RL with no cold-start SFT or mid-training stage.
The learned search behavior transfers to open-web benchmarks, and training curves show earlier improvement and faster convergence than outcome-only RL.
content_html: Multi-turn agents that chain together tool calls for tens or hundreds of steps before answering face a hard credit-assignment problem: outcome-only rewards get sparse and noisy as trajectories stretch out, and a rollout that ultimately fails can still contain plenty of individually useful actions that outcome-only training punishes just as harshly as the actual mistake.
extra_html:
Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, and colleagues propose TRACE (Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation), a dense credit-assignment method for agentic RL. TRACE represents each rollout as a sequence of state transitions at tool-call boundaries, pulls gold-answer log-probabilities from a frozen reference model, and converts those into log-ratio state values. Per-action rewards then fall out as the Temporal-Difference change in that value from one turn to the next — a one-step log-ratio TD term that telescopes cleanly across redundant tool calls, with no additional critic network or process-label training required.

On the closed-web BrowseComp-Plus benchmark, TRACE substantially improves tool-use ability with pure RL alone — no cold-start supervised fine-tuning, no agentic mid-training stage, and no live-web training data — lifting Qwen3-4B from 7.2 to 35.6 and Qwen3-30B-A3B from 8.4 to 42.6. The resulting search behavior also transfers to open-web benchmarks, and training curves show earlier improvement and faster convergence than outcome-only baselines. Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, and colleagues, arXiv, July 2026.

related.title: ZPPO: Put the Teacher in the Prompt, Not the Gradient
related.hook: A small student learns from a bigger teacher without the drift that breaks on-policy RL - by feeding the teacher's answer into the prompt as a candidate to judge, never into the gradient.

flashcards.prompt: Why does outcome-only reward become a problem for long-horizon, multi-turn agents specifically?
flashcards.back_html: Over tens to hundreds of tool calls, outcome rewards get sparse and high-variance, and a failed rollout's useful early actions get the same negative signal as the eventual mistake that caused failure.

flashcards.prompt: How does TRACE turn a frozen reference model's gold-answer log-probabilities into per-action rewards?

choices.text: It converts them into log-ratio state values, then takes the Temporal-Difference change in that value across each tool-call boundary as the reward
It trains a separate learned critic network to score each action
It asks a human annotator to label each tool call as helpful or not

flashcards.explanation_html: TRACE needs no extra critic or process-label training — the reward comes from the TD change in log-ratio state values derived from a frozen reference model's log-probabilities.

flashcards.prompt: How much did TRACE improve Qwen3-4B on the closed-web BrowseComp-Plus benchmark?
flashcards.explanation_html: Pure RL with TRACE raised Qwen3-4B from 7.2 to 35.6 on BrowseComp-Plus, and Qwen3-30B-A3B from 8.4 to 42.6 — with no cold-start SFT stage.
